subject: Maths
title: Cumulative frequency and box plots
subtitle: Statistics · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can draw and interpret cumulative frequency diagrams and box plots.

key_vocab.definition: Cumulative frequency is the running total of frequencies. A box plot (box-and-whisker diagram) displays the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median (Q2), upper quartile (Q3), and maximum.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can draw and interpret cumulative frequency diagrams and box plots.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Cumulative frequency -- Cumulative frequency is the running total of frequencies. A box plot (box-and-whisker diagram) displays the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median (Q2), upper quartile (Q3), and maximum.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Cumulative frequency = running total. Read quartiles from the CF graph. IQR = Q3 − Q1.
IQR = Q3 − Q1
The interquartile range measures spread of the middle 50% of data

Key examples:
  ✓ IQR = Q3 − Q1 measures the spread of middle 50%  (interquartile range)
  ✓ Median is at the &frac{n}{2} position on the CF curve  (reading the median)
  ✓ Box plot shows min, Q1, Q2, Q3, max  (five-number summary)
  ✗ Plot CF against midpoints  (plot against upper boundaries)
  ✗ IQR = Q3 + Q1  (IQR = Q3 MINUS Q1)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – building a CF table
  Frequencies are 5, 8, 12, 10, 5. Build the cumulative frequency column.
  CF: 5, 5+8=13, 13+12=25, 25+10=35, 35+5=40
  Total n = 40
  CF values: 5, 13, 25, 35, 40
  5, 13, 25, 35, 40
  (Add each frequency to the running total.)

Example 2 – reading the median
  n = 40. Read the median from the CF graph.
  Median position: &frac{40}{2} = 20th value
  Go across from CF = 20 to the curve
  Read down to the x-axis for the median
  Read at CF = 20
  (The median is the value at the &frac{n}{2} position on the y-axis.)

sections.title: Building CF tables
sections.content:
Find the cumulative frequencies.

(a) Frequencies: 3, 7, 10, 5, 5
(b) Frequencies: 4, 6, 15, 8, 7
(c) Frequencies: 2, 8, 12, 14, 4
(d) Frequencies: 10, 15, 20, 10, 5

sections.title: Finding quartile positions
sections.content:
State the CF positions for Q1, Q2, Q3.

(a) n = 40
(b) n = 60
(c) n = 100
(d) n = 80

sections.title: Calculating IQR
sections.content:
Find the IQR from the given quartiles.

(a) Q1 = 15, Q3 = 35
(b) Q1 = 42, Q3 = 68
(c) Q1 = 3.5, Q3 = 7.2
(d) Q1 = 120, Q3 = 185

sections.title: Box plot interpretation
sections.content:
From the box plot, find the stated value.

(a) Min=10, Q1=20, Q2=35, Q3=50, Max=70. Range?
(b) Same data. IQR?
(c) Min=5, Q1=12, Q2=18, Q3=25, Max=40. Median?
(d) Same data. What fraction is between Q1 and Q3?

sections.title: Comparing distributions
sections.content:
Compare using the given statistics.

(a) Set A: median 45, IQR 20. Set B: median 52, IQR 35. Which has higher average?
(b) Same data. Which is more consistent?
(c) Boys: Q1=55, Q3=75. Girls: Q1=60, Q3=70. Compare.
(d) Dataset: min=3, Q1=5, Q2=7, Q3=9, max=15. Is it symmetric?
(e) If IQR = 0, what does this tell you?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ IQR = Q3 − Q1
✗ CF should be plotted against class midpoints
✓ The median is read at the &frac{n}{2} position on the CF graph
✗ The box in a box plot always shows 25% of the data
✓ A box plot shows the five-number summary: min, Q1, Q2, Q3, max
